stories.title: Eurozone inflation rises to a three-year high of 4.0%.
stories.dek: An energy-led rise in prices is keeping rate-hike risks in focus.
body: Eurozone inflation accelerated to 4.0% in October from 3.8% in September, its highest rate in three years, according to flash data reported on Wednesday. Higher energy prices were cited as the driver, adding to expectations of further European Central Bank tightening.

sources.title: Eurozone Inflation Accelerates To 3-Year High On Energy Prices

stories.title: Eurozone growth slowed to a four-month low in October.
stories.dek: Expansion persisted, but demand nearly stalled as cost pressures intensified.
body: The eurozone composite PMI fell to 51.7 in October from 53.1 in September, a four-month low and below the preliminary 51.9 reading. The services PMI eased to 51.4 from 53.0, while input-price inflation reached a five-month high and business confidence weakened.

sources.title: Euro zone economic growth slows to four-month low in October, PMI shows

stories.title: UK services growth reached an eight-month high, while cost pressures rose.
stories.dek: Activity improved, but rising costs complicate the outlook ahead of the BoE decision.
body: UK services activity strengthened: the October PMI rose to 52.8 from 52.1, its highest reading since February, while the composite index increased to 52.9 from 52.0. The services figure was below the flash estimate of 53.1; input-price inflation accelerated to its highest since May, adding to expectations of Bank of England tightening.

sources.title: UK services growth hits 8-month high in October, PMI shows

stories.title: European stocks rebounded as banks and clean-energy shares outperformed.
stories.dek: Banks and clean-energy shares led a European rebound after Democrats took both chambers of Congress.
body: European shares recovered from early losses as investors assessed the US midterm result. The STOXX 600 was up 0.5% at 0816 GMT, with banks gaining more than 2%; clean-energy stocks also advanced, including Ørsted, up 7%, and Vestas, up 5%. Novo Nordisk rose after lifting its annual outlook.

sources.title: European shares rise as Democratic sweep lifts clean energy, bank stocks

stories.title: Novo Nordisk lifted its 2026 outlook again after Wegovy pill sales beat forecasts.
stories.dek: Stronger obesity-drug sales prompted a third upgrade to the company’s full-year outlook.
body: Novo Nordisk raised its 2026 adjusted sales and operating-profit growth outlook to a range of -2% to +2% at constant exchange rates, from its previous -6% to 0% range. Third-quarter adjusted operating profit was 31.72 billion Danish crowns, above the 28.39 billion analyst consensus; Wegovy pill sales were 5.39 billion crowns. Shares rose as much as 6.6% in early trading.

sources.title: Novo Nordisk hikes 2026 outlook again as Wegovy pill beats forecasts

stories.title: AMD rallied in premarket after forecasting faster growth through 2027.
stories.dek: The outlook offered investors evidence that AI infrastructure demand extends beyond accelerator chips.
body: AMD forecast overall revenue growth of more than 80% in 2027, ahead of analysts’ 77% estimate, as demand for data-centre processors and AI computing strengthens. Third-quarter data-centre revenue rose 97% to $8.55 billion, beating expectations of $8.20 billion. The stock was up 7.3% in premarket trading.

sources.title: AMD shares jump as AI-driven data-center strength fuels growth outlook

stories.title: BMW’s quarterly pretax earnings fell 11% as China sales weakened.
stories.dek: Weak China sales and restructuring costs cloud the outlook despite an in-line earnings result.
body: BMW reported third-quarter pretax earnings of €2.1 billion, down 11% year on year and in line with analysts’ expectations. Revenue fell 6% to €30.4 billion, with declining sales in China weighing on results; the automotive operating margin narrowed to 3.4% from 5.2% a year earlier. The company also warned restructuring costs would hit later-year results.

sources.title: BMW warns on profit again as restructuring costs bite

stories.title: Fresenius raised its 2026 earnings expectations after a strong quarter.
stories.dek: Kabi and Helios performance supported the healthcare group’s second outlook increase this year.
body: Fresenius raised its 2026 expectations after stronger-than-anticipated third-quarter results. It now expects constant-currency core EPS growth at the upper end of its 10%-15% range and an EBIT margin above 11.5%. Third-quarter EBIT before special items was €638 million, above the €618.5 million consensus.

sources.title: Fresenius lifts 2026 expectations after strong Q3

stories.title: US futures recovered as markets digested a Democratic sweep of Congress.
stories.dek: The election outcome initially unsettled risk assets, but futures pared losses before the US open.
body: US Treasury yields slipped and the dollar weakened as investors weighed Democrats’ control of both chambers of Congress and the possibility of policy gridlock. US equity futures recovered from sharp initial losses: Nasdaq-100 futures had fallen as much as 2.4% and S&P 500 futures 1.4% before stabilising. Markets were also watching Treasury refunding details and the week’s labour-market reports.

sources.title: US stock index futures steady as Democrats seize Congress
Stocks rally, dollar dips after Democrats' midterm sweep

stories.title: Bitcoin rebounded after briefly touching a six-week low on the US election result.
stories.dek: The initial election-driven dip eased, though broader crypto sentiment remained fragile.
body: Bitcoin briefly fell to a six-week low as Democrats won control of the Senate and House, raising uncertainty around the industry’s deregulatory agenda, then recovered. It was trading around $78,070 by 0715 GMT, roughly flat at the time; ether was at $2,292, up about 1%. The move came amid wider concern over risk appetite and the recent Binance hack.

sources.title: Crypto dips on Democrat midterm wins, Binance hack dent optimism
Bitcoin Slips as Democratic Sweep Bets Threaten Crypto Agenda

stories.title: Iran strikes revive oil-market nerves after Monday’s plunge
stories.dek: Reports of US strikes on Iran revived supply concerns after oil’s sharp fall a day earlier.
body: Brent crude rebounded above $100 a barrel after the previous session’s roughly 7% drop, as reports of US strikes on Iran’s Qeshm Island unsettled markets and cast doubt on the prospects for de-escalation. The strikes were described by US officials as defensive.
The renewed tension around the Strait of Hormuz put energy supply risks back in focus as investors also watched for developments in US-Iran talks.

sources.title: Morning Bid: So much for a quiet day before the US midterms
COMMENTARY: Midterms and mediation

stories.title: European stocks slip as tech fears meet renewed Iran tensions
stories.dek: AI-trade worries and Middle East tensions weighed on European risk appetite, while Drax jumped on a data-centre deal.
body: European shares were lower as investors weighed concerns about the returns on heavy AI spending against reports of escalating Middle East tensions. The STOXX 600 was down 0.4% at 647.13 by 0955 GMT, with technology stocks falling 1.6%.

ASML and STMicroelectronics were among the tech stocks under pressure. Drax stood out, rising 9% after announcing a partnership to develop a data centre project that could attract more than £20 billion in investment.

sources.title: Europe stocks slip on AI concerns, escalating Iran tensions

stories.title: Bayer raises 2026 profit outlook on pharma strength
stories.dek: Stronger pharmaceutical performance prompted the German group to lift its full-year earnings range.
body: Bayer raised its 2026 adjusted EBITDA outlook to €9.8 billion–€10.3 billion from €9.6 billion–€10.1 billion, citing better-than-expected pharmaceutical performance. Its pharma business recorded third-quarter sales of €4.68 billion, 5% above analysts’ expectations in a Vara Research poll.

The group also lowered its expected year-end net financial debt range by €1 billion, to €28 billion–€29 billion. Its crop-science division’s adjusted core earnings were €101 million, below analysts’ €164 million estimate.

sources.title: Bayer hikes 2026 profit outlook as pharma unit beats expectations

stories.title: AB Foods warns of another profit decline as sugar losses deepen
stories.dek: Lower Primark profitability and deeper sugar losses dragged on earnings, with another profit decline forecast.
body: Associated British Foods reported adjusted operating profit of £1.508 billion for the year to September 12, down 13% in reported currency and 14% at constant currency. Revenue was £19.58 billion, down 1% at constant currency, while adjusted earnings per share fell 11% to 156.0p.

The Primark owner expects adjusted operating profit and adjusted EPS to fall again in 2026/27, mainly because of its sugar business. Sugar recorded a £47 million loss in the year just ended, and ABF expects that loss to widen to £70 million–£170 million.

sources.title: Primark-owner AB Foods forecasts further profit decline as sugar losses deepen
2026 Annual Results Announcement

stories.title: Philips beats on adjusted profit and reaches preliminary DOJ agreement
stories.dek: An adjusted profit beat and a preliminary DOJ agreement supported the Dutch medtech group.
body: Philips said third-quarter adjusted EBITA rose 7.2% to €569 million, ahead of analysts’ €522 million estimate, while comparable sales increased 3% to €4.39 billion, slightly below forecasts.

The company also reached a preliminary agreement with the US Department of Justice to resolve investigations connected to its 2021 global recall of sleep and respiratory-care devices. Philips reiterated its 2026 financial targets.

sources.title: Philips reaches DOJ agreement over device recall, books €288 million provision in Q3

stories.title: Lufthansa rises despite trimming its annual profit forecast
stories.dek: Investors appeared to look past a lower annual profit outlook to resilient results.
body: Lufthansa shares rose 3.3% even as the airline trimmed its annual profit forecast. Reuters cited analysts’ view that the company’s results were broadly resilient.
The move came against a weaker European market, where investors were focused on technology valuations and Middle East tensions.

sources.title: Europe stocks slip on AI concerns, escalating Iran tensions

stories.title: Apple slides in premarket after warning of holiday-quarter margin pressure
stories.dek: A margin warning overshadowed the iPhone maker’s earnings beat in premarket trading.
body: Apple shares fell 4.5% in premarket trading after the company warned that higher memory-chip costs would pressure gross margin in the holiday quarter, overshadowing stronger-than-expected results and iPhone sales.
The weakness added to investor concerns about profitability across big technology companies, even as markets awaited US midterm election results.

sources.title: S&P 500, Nasdaq set for higher open as oil prices extend declines, midterm results awaited

stories.title: Palantir falls before the open despite upbeat sales guidance
stories.dek: Strong results and an above-consensus sales forecast failed to prevent a premarket decline.
body: Palantir shares fell 6.3% in premarket trading, although the software company forecast fourth-quarter revenue above analysts’ estimates after beating third-quarter expectations.
Investors were unconvinced by the outlook: Reuters reported that the shares fell despite the upbeat revenue forecast, amid broader concern about technology valuations and AI spending.

sources.title: S&P 500, Nasdaq set for higher open as oil prices extend declines, midterm results awaited

stories.title: Bitcoin extends losses to a one-month low near $76,500
stories.dek: Election uncertainty and the fallout from the Binance theft weighed on bitcoin and broader crypto sentiment.
body: Bitcoin traded near $76,500 in early trading, down about 2% and at its lowest level in more than a month, as caution ahead of the US midterms added to pressure on digital assets.

The market was also contending with the fallout from the reported $6.3 billion Binance theft and recent outflows from spot bitcoin funds. Binance said it would cover customer losses and had resumed withdrawals at a staggered pace.

sources.title: Bitcoin slips to over 1-mth low of $76.5k as U.S. midterm caution weighs

stories.title: AI spending fears deepen the global tech selloff
stories.dek: AI-spending jitters drove a broad tech-led selloff, with US indexes sharply lower in early trading.
body: European shares fell as renewed concern about returns on heavy AI investment weighed on technology stocks. The STOXX 600 was down around 0.3% in morning trading, though it remained on track for a monthly gain.
US futures also pointed lower, with S&P 500 e-minis down 0.89% in Reuters’ morning report. After the open, the S&P 500 fell 1.16% and the Nasdaq dropped 2.26%, while the Dow edged up 0.08%.

sources.title: Tech giants' spending spooks investors as bonds rally
Nasdaq tumbles at open as Amazon, Intel add to AI spending woes

stories.title: Euro-zone growth beats forecasts as inflation risks persist
stories.dek: The bloc’s growth beat expectations, but uneven national results and rising price pressures cloud the policy picture.
body: Euro-zone GDP grew 0.4% quarter on quarter in the third quarter, slowing from 0.6% in the previous quarter but exceeding the 0.2% growth economists had forecast.

Germany expanded 0.2%, Spain and the Netherlands each grew 0.6%, Italy was flat and France contracted 0.1%. Separate national inflation readings showed price growth accelerating in several major euro-zone economies, complicating the outlook for the ECB.

sources.title: Euro zone growth beats projections again

stories.title: German inflation cools more than expected
stories.dek: A larger-than-expected slowdown in German prices offered some relief amid wider euro-area inflation concerns.
body: Germany’s harmonised inflation rate slowed to 2.8% year on year in October, from 3.3% in September and below the 3.1% expected by economists polled by Reuters.
The first month of a fuel-tax cut helped ease pump-price pressures. Core inflation also declined, to 2.1% from 2.4%.

sources.title: German inflation slows more than expected in October

stories.title: ECB survey finds more euro-zone firms anticipate wage pressure
stories.dek: The survey adds to the ECB’s focus on whether the energy-driven inflation rise will feed into wages.
body: The ECB’s quarterly survey of large euro-zone companies found that 40% expected or saw a risk of higher wage demands, up from 20% in the previous survey in July.

Companies still expected wage growth to slow, from 3.2% last year to 3.0% this year and 2.9% next year, but at a more gradual pace than previously anticipated. The survey also pointed to continued cost pressures, including from energy and agricultural prices.

sources.title: Euro zone companies brace for higher wage demands, ECB poll shows

stories.title: US labour costs rise at a slower pace in the third quarter
stories.dek: A moderation in quarterly labour-cost growth offered a counterpoint to recent US inflation concerns.
body: US employment costs rose 0.8% in the third quarter, matching economists’ expectations but slowing from a 0.9% increase in the second quarter, according to the Employment Cost Index.
Wages and salaries rose 0.7% in the quarter, also slower than the prior period. Total labour costs were up 3.4% over the year to September, while inflation-adjusted wages fell 0.6%.

sources.title: Slower wage growth curbs US labor costs in third quarter

stories.title: BP posts $8.46 billion quarterly profit and reaches debt target early
stories.dek: Higher energy prices and refining margins lifted BP’s profit to a record under its current reporting measure.
body: BP reported third-quarter underlying replacement-cost profit of $8.46 billion, above the $7.33 billion expected by analysts and up from $2.2 billion a year earlier. The company said its quarterly operating cash flow was $14.8 billion.

Net debt fell to $13.9 billion, allowing BP to reach its net-debt target a year early. The company said it would use the windfall to settle its remaining Deepwater Horizon liabilities; its shares were up about 0.5% in morning trading.

sources.title: BP beats third-quarter forecasts with record $8.46 billion profit

stories.title: Sanofi lifts its 2026 outlook again as quarterly profit beats forecasts
stories.dek: A strong quarter and upgraded guidance lifted the French drugmaker’s shares, while its new CEO flagged dealmaking ambitions.
body: Sanofi raised its 2026 targets for the second time this year, projecting low-teens sales growth and mid-teens growth in business earnings per share at constant exchange rates.

Third-quarter business operating income was €5.43 billion, ahead of the €4.32 billion analyst consensus cited by Reuters. The French drugmaker’s shares rose nearly 6% to their highest level since April as it also signalled interest in acquisitions to replenish its pipeline.

sources.title: Sanofi teases appetite for larger deals, lifts 2026 growth targets under new CEO Garijo
Q3 2026: double-digit growth in sales and business EPS; 2026 guidance upgraded

stories.title: Puma gains as results point to progress in its turnaround
stories.dek: Quarterly results and its product rollout helped the sportswear group stand out in a weak European market.
body: Puma shares advanced after the German sportswear company reported third-quarter sales that Reuters said were in line with estimates, supporting signs of progress in its turnaround.
Reuters’ European-market report put the shares up 4% in one update; a later market report recorded a gain of 6.9%.

sources.title: European shares drop as AI spending worries hit tech; though best month since June in sight
Stock Movers: BP, Sanofi, Puma

stories.title: Bayer rises after winning Roundup cancer-claims trial
stories.dek: A courtroom win gave Bayer a lift amid its long-running Roundup litigation overhang.
body: Bayer rose after winning a trial on Thursday involving claims by three women that its Roundup weedkiller caused their cancer. Reuters reported the shares up 4.1% in European trading.
The court outcome offered a positive legal development for the company as investors weighed ongoing litigation exposure.

sources.title: European shares ease as AI-driven tech selloff deepens

stories.title: Binance says partners have located about $3 billion in affected assets
stories.dek: Asset freezes covered roughly half the reported haul, but crypto prices remained under pressure as the recovery picture stayed incomplete.
body: Following the reported Binance security incident, the exchange said it and its partners had located about $3 billion of the estimated $6.3 billion in affected assets; Reuters reported that it gave no update on the remaining $3.3 billion.

Bitcoin reached a six-week low and was last down about 3% in Reuters’ market update, while ether was down more than 3%. Reuters also reported that stablecoin issuers had frozen roughly half of the stolen assets.

sources.title: Analysts react as Binance freezes assets after $6.3 billion security breach
Explainer: Gone in 20 minutes: How the biggest heist in crypto history unfolded

stories.title: Intel sinks about a quarter as a PC slump and weak outlook overshadow AI growth
stories.dek: Fourth-quarter revenue guidance of $15–16bn came in well below the roughly $17.1bn analysts expected.
body: Intel guided fourth-quarter revenue to $15bn–$16bn, below both the third quarter’s $16.5bn and the consensus of about $17.1bn. It expects adjusted gross margin to fall to 38% from 44.1%, and adjusted EPS of about $0.25 against roughly $0.43 expected.

PC revenue fell 5% to $8.1bn while data-centre and AI revenue rose 78%. Management said PC weakness would last at least through the first half of next year, and also pointed to a factory accident in Israel.
The shares were down about 25% before the US open, dragging chipmakers in Asia and Europe lower.

sources.title: Stock Market Today Live, October 30, 2026
Stock Market Today, Oct. 30, 2026

stories.title: Amazon misses on earnings as AI spending pushes free cash flow negative
stories.dek: AWS grew 39%, but trailing free cash flow swung to about minus $42.4bn.
body: Third-quarter sales rose 12% to $201.9bn and AWS grew 39%, but earnings per share of $1.89 missed the $1.96 estimate and sales were slightly light.
Trailing twelve-month free cash flow turned negative at about −$42.4bn as Amazon lifted its 2026 capital spending plan to around $220bn, much of it on AI infrastructure.
The shares fell about 7% before the open, feeding the wider debate over whether AI capex is earning a return.

sources.title: Stock Market Today Live, October 30, 2026
Live updates: Binance hack rattles crypto as Intel plunges and AI spending fears hit tech

stories.title: Binance hit by an estimated $6.3bn hack, likely crypto’s largest theft
stories.dek: About $3bn has been frozen; Binance says it will cover all losses and reopen withdrawals within two days.
body: Binance halted withdrawals after attackers drained an estimated $6.3bn. Around $3bn has been frozen with blockchain partners and law enforcement, and investigators have linked the attack to North Korea.
The exchange first pointed to a compromised employee laptop, then said it had found further points of breach. It has set aside about $6.34bn to make customers whole and says deposits were unaffected.
Bitcoin dropped below $77,000 and ether fell nearly 6%, with roughly $1.5bn of leveraged positions liquidated.

sources.title: Live updates: Bitcoin falls to $77,000 as Binance exploit combines with tech woes
Stock Market Today, Oct. 30, 2026

stories.title: Brent climbs toward $118 as tanker attacks keep Hormuz risk alive
stories.dek: Iran claimed mine strikes on commercial vessels even as Washington said the war would end soon.
body: Brent rose about 2.5% to near $117.80 a barrel and WTI to about $104 after reports of attacks on tankers and Houthi claims of strikes on Saudi Arabia.
President Trump said the conflict with Iran would end soon without saying how, while US Central Command said southern shipping lanes were open. Qatari mediators returned to Tehran.
Traders are also weighing the risk of renewed fighting around the 3 November US midterm elections.

sources.title: Stock Market Today, Oct. 30, 2026

stories.title: AstraZeneca beats third-quarter forecasts and keeps full-year guidance
stories.dek: Pre-tax profit rose 22% to $3.96bn on revenue of $16.21bn.
body: Revenue rose 6.7% to $16.21bn and pre-tax profit climbed 22% to $3.96bn, both ahead of market expectations. Full-year guidance was unchanged.
The shares rose almost 4%, one of the main supports for the FTSE 100 on a weak day for growth stocks elsewhere.

sources.title: FTSE 100 rises as BT and AstraZeneca rally but NatWest plunges 7.4%
FTSE 100 edges up as EU growth beats forecasts

stories.title: NatWest falls 7% as net interest income misses and AI-led job cuts reach 1,400
stories.dek: Attributable profit slipped 4.1% to £1.53bn; the full-year outlook was kept.
body: Net interest income rose 8.9% to £3.56bn but missed analyst forecasts, and profit attributable to shareholders fell 4.1% to £1.53bn.
The bank said about 1,400 roles have gone this year, around 1,000 of them in the quarter, as AI changes how it operates. Its full-year outlook was reaffirmed.
NatWest was the biggest drag on the FTSE 100 by midday.

sources.title: FTSE 100 rises as BT and AstraZeneca rally but NatWest plunges 7.4%
FTSE 100 edges up as EU growth beats forecasts

stories.title: Mobico agrees £308m cash takeover by Leita Mobility at a 55% premium
stories.dek: The 46p-a-share offer values the bus and coach operator at about £2.32bn including debt.
body: Mobico backed a cash offer of 46p a share from Leita Mobility, part of Spain’s Autobuses de León, a 55% premium to the 20 October close of 29.7p.
Including debt, the deal values the group at around £2.32bn. It is expected to complete through a court-sanctioned scheme. The shares rose about 12%.

sources.title: FTSE 100 rises as BT and AstraZeneca rally but NatWest plunges 7.4%
FTSE 100 edges up as EU growth beats forecasts

stories.title: Sandisk falls despite a revenue beat and an eight-for-one split
stories.dek: Investors worry memory pricing is close to a peak.
body: Fiscal first-quarter revenue rose 23% to $11.03bn, above the company’s own forecast, and Sandisk announced an eight-for-one stock split.
The shares still fell nearly 8% before the open as investors questioned how long strong memory prices can last.

stories.title: Reddit and Twilio slump on softer outlooks
stories.dek: Reddit’s US daily users fell 2% despite 53% revenue growth; Twilio guided growth lower.
body: Reddit grew revenue 53% and beat on earnings, but a weaker fourth-quarter revenue outlook and a 2% drop in US daily active users sent the shares down more than 20%.
Twilio guided fourth-quarter revenue growth to 17%–17.5% after 20% in the third quarter, and fell around 20% before the open.

stories.title: France’s economy shrinks 0.1% as inflation rises to 3.4%
stories.dek: The 10-year OAT yield rose to about 4.97%.
body: French GDP fell 0.1% in the third quarter while inflation climbed to 3.4%, a stagflationary mix that pushed the 10-year OAT yield up to about 4.97%.

stories.title: BT jumps on report Virgin Media O2 is close to an Openreach fibre deal
stories.dek: Neither company has confirmed the talks.
body: BT rose almost 6% after reports that Virgin Media O2 is nearing an agreement to use Openreach’s fibre network outside its own footprint, while pausing some of its own cable upgrades to save costs. Neither company has confirmed a deal.

stories.title: Alphabet has its worst day on record after an earnings miss
stories.dek: Adjusted EPS of $2.12 missed consensus by about 28%; free cash flow was about −$9.1bn.
body: Search revenue of $63.4bn fell short of the $64.9bn expected, and free cash flow came in at about −$9.1bn against −$3.5bn forecast. The shares fell 12.6%, pulling the Nasdaq down 1.4%.

stories.title: ServiceNow and Fortinet tumble on soft forward indicators
stories.dek: ServiceNow posted its worst day on record.
body: ServiceNow fell 27% after guiding fourth-quarter remaining performance obligation growth to 18.5% against 19.4% expected. Fortinet dropped 20% after trimming its full-year service revenue forecast below consensus.

stories.title: US economy grew 3.4% annualised in Q3; core PCE rose 0.3%
stories.dek: Growth beat the 3.2% estimate while monthly core inflation came in below forecast.
body: Third-quarter GDP beat the 3.2% estimate. Core PCE rose 0.3% in September, below the 0.4% forecast, for 3.1% year on year, while headline PCE ran at 3.6%. Weekly jobless claims fell to 194,000.

stories.title: Fed holds rates at 3.75%–4% as two officials vote for a hike
stories.dek: Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack dissented in favour of tightening.
body: The Federal Reserve under Chair Kevin Warsh left its target range at 3.75%–4%, with Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack voting for an increase. After the press conference, futures priced a December hike at close to 90%.
